summary: This lecture, part 130 of Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter), focuses on the miracles of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) beyond the Quran. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that the Quran itself is the greatest miracle, possessing eloquence, wisdom, accuracy, and timeless relevance that proves its divine origin. The lecture then discusses several miracles attributed to the Prophet, with particular attention to the splitting of the moon (Inshiqaq), which is mentioned in the Quran and witnessed by the people of Mecca. Sh. Ali Mashhour addresses modern skepticism about this miracle, explaining that while some attempt to rationalize it through natural means, the scholars and companions unanimously affirmed this event occurred during the Prophet's lifetime. The lecture warns against trivializing miracles or accepting false miracle claims that cheapen the Islamic narrative, such as viral videos of animals appearing to write Arabic letters.
